correctness.rationale: The unique missing colour at each endpoint is the only viable alternative, so matching missing colours characterize the legal moves. I enumerated proper colourings by first-use-ordered classes, expanded over all 24 palettes after verifying that every partition uses four classes, bucketed colourings by deletion of one edge coordinate to form all transitions, and computed components by BFS. The result was 49920 states, 109440 edges, 960 singletons and two components of 24480, with the full frozen degree histogram reproduced. Explicit symbol and palette actions gave one frozen orbit and the asserted sign action on the two mobile components. Replay: python3 branches/independent_petersen.py. This is exact for four named colours and one-edge moves only.

evidence: The product of the ten local permutation signs is invariant under palette relabelling (factor sign(palette)^10). Reordering incident edges under any symbol permutation multiplies the product by a factor independent of colouring. This gives a homomorphism to {+1,-1}; the reported sign swap by a transposition makes the homomorphism the ordinary sign.

The same source gives exactly two A5 x S4 frozen orbits, and 480 frozen states of each sign. Each of these orbits has a constant sign, so an odd symbol permutation interchanges the two and the full group is transitive on the frozen states.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Together with completeness of sign on the mobile states, the stronger result entails the assigned symmetry claims, even where not phrased as the same orbit statement.

evidence: Proper edge-colourings correspond to vertex colourings of the Petersen line graph, with the same one-coordinate moves. Osawa et al. define the one-edge move. The local-sign record uses the identical four named colours and excludes simultaneous multiedge changes.
McDonald–Mohar–Scheide's Kempe move switches alternating paths or cycles and is strictly stronger here; its connectivity result does not cover this state graph.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The line-graph reduction preserves the transitions; replacing single-edge moves by Kempe exchanges does not. The exact mirror overlap is under the correct, weaker move.

originality.rationale: The distinct indexed Petersen local-sign and distance result gives the same census, degree distribution and frozen criterion and implies the claimed group actions, including the full frozen orbit. Thus the assigned scientific content is covered by a stronger result in the examined catalogue. The indexed result has a later date label than the frozen record; this decision is about demonstrable coverage in the current evidence, not a finding about which came first or whether they were developed independently. No independent scientific remainder in the frozen finding was established.
residual_risks: The compared catalogue date labels do not establish priority, derivation or independence.
